chapter: Fellow musicians: Kirk, Bunk, Parker, McShann
title: Jay McShann's band in New York and Al Hibbler
summary: Goodwin tells how, in the service, a soldier's mention of a blind singer made him think of Walter Brown, not Al Hibbler.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: He went to New York with Jay McShann's band in New York in 1941?
Oh, what happened to Jay McShann's band in New York in 1941?

They had -- Al Hibler, you know, was with Jay McShann, because I was in the service then and a fellow from New York was in my company in the service and I had told this fellow that -- he was a clarinet player -- I told him, I said, "I know Jay McShann very well", and he said, "Well who is this guy that they had to lead to the microphone to sing"?
Well, I didn't know that Al Hibler was with Jay.
You didn't know Al Hibler in Kansas City?
No, I have -- I had never met him. I hadn't heard of him but what I thought, he had a singer, a blues singer with him, Walter Brown --
-- and it first came to my mind that Walter Brown had gone blind.
Well, I had no way of knowing. I was in the service. I'm out of connection. See, I had lost contact with the fellows.
And you thought Walter Brown had gone blind?
I thought, I said, 'Well it must have been Walter Brown' because this guy he didn't know Al Hibbler either because Al Hibbler was famous then.
Basie, of course, did a lot for Al Hibbler.
See, he sang with the Duke, but he was a beautiful.
But Jay keeps going on and on with that Territory Band making albums. He just made one in New York not too long ago and he was at the party Sunday night. Did you see him there?
